description: A SaaS platform for Kenyan matatu (public transit) fleet management, built for SACCOs and transport operators. Combines real-time GPS tracking via Hyperledger Fabric ledger events, M-Pesa subscription billing, role-based operator/driver/passenger onboarding, and compliance-grade trip analytics — serving the full transit value chain from ORG_CHAIRs and fleet owners to regulators and urban planners.

evidence: Platform serves Kenyan matatu SACCOs with role types: ORG_CHAIR, DRIVER, CONDUCTOR, ROUTE_SUPERVISOR, DISPATCHER, REGULATOR, COMPLIANCE_OFFICER, PLANNER
M-Pesa (Safaricom Daraja) is the primary payment processor — strongly signals Kenyan market focus
MapLibre and h3-js geospatial stack used for real-time GPS fleet tracking and route visualization
Hyperledger Fabric integration provides compliance-grade immutable ledger for trip and GPS events
Blog content references NTSA compliance, empty return trips, and Nairobi matatu operations — confirming transit vertical
Revenue config includes reservation fees, platform take rates, and tipping splits consistent with a transit marketplace model
Pricing plans reference vehicle limits, route alerts, and geofences — core fleet management SaaS features
B2G signal: dedicated dashboards for REGULATOR and PLANNER roles with no current pricing tier, suggesting government/institutional buyer segment

current_growth_features.detected_intent: Enables viral growth through secure role-based invitations. Operators and org chairs can invite members to join their SACCO organization with pre-assigned roles, driving network expansion through trusted referrals.
growth_potential: Add PostHog tracking for invite funnel: token_viewed → account_created → role_activated to measure conversion rates
Implement bulk invite capability so ORG_CHAIRs can onboard entire crews at once
Add invite expiry extension flow — currently hard-fails at 72h with no recovery path, losing warm leads
Send a welcome email sequence post-redemption to accelerate new member activation
Surface invite acceptance rate in the admin dashboard as a SACCO health metric
Add SMS-based invite delivery for users without email access (critical in Kenyan market)

current_growth_features.detected_intent: Facilitates operator onboarding by allowing users to self-select and claim ownership of pre-seeded SACCO organizations. This is the primary top-of-funnel activation path for the ORG_CHAIR role, which anchors the entire organizational growth loop.
growth_potential: Add PostHog event on join request submission to measure drop-off between org selection and form completion
Implement email/SMS notification to admin when a new join request arrives to reduce approval latency
Add a status page at /org/join-status so applicants can track their pending request without contacting support
Pre-populate org selection via URL param (?org_id=) from marketing campaigns or QR codes at SACCO offices
Add a 'request new SACCO' path for operators whose organization isn't listed, capturing demand signal
Show estimated approval time on the join-success page to set expectations and reduce support tickets

current_growth_features.detected_intent: Drives user activation by enabling admins to approve pending role requests. Approval latency directly determines how quickly new operators, drivers, and conductors become active — making this a critical retention lever. Slow approval is a churn trigger.
growth_potential: Add push/email notification to admin when queue depth exceeds a threshold (e.g. >5 pending requests)
Track time-to-approval in PostHog to surface bottlenecks — p50/p95 approval latency as a platform health KPI
Add bulk approve capability for common patterns (e.g. approve all pending org_member requests for a specific SACCO)
Implement auto-approval rules for low-risk request types (e.g. passenger role) to reduce admin burden
Send approval confirmation SMS/email to the applicant immediately on approval to drive re-engagement
Add a rejection reason template library so admins can reject with helpful guidance rather than leaving users stranded

current_growth_features.detected_intent: Drives retention and upgrade conversion by surfacing revenue variance, route performance, and reconciliation data. The more value operators see in this dashboard, the stronger the case for maintaining a paid subscription. Acts as the primary data-driven decision tool for ORG_CHAIRs.
growth_potential: Add PostHog pageview and interaction events to measure which dashboard sections drive the most engagement
Implement weekly email digest of key metrics (total collected, variance, top route) to drive re-engagement without requiring login
Add a 'route optimization suggestion' card when variance is consistently negative — creates upgrade urgency
Surface a comparison view (this week vs last week) to make improvement visible and reinforce platform value
Add CSV/PDF export for reconciliation data — compliance reporting is a key retention driver for SACCO managers
Add anomaly alerts (e.g. 'Vehicle KDG 123X collected 40% below target today') via SMS to drive daily active use

current_growth_features.detected_intent: Enables data-driven monetization decisions by surfacing platform revenue, M-Pesa subscription counts, B2C payouts, and Hyperledger enrollment health in one view. Supports identifying revenue leakage and subscriber growth trends.
growth_potential: Add month-over-month subscriber growth trend chart to make subscription growth visible at a glance
Surface churn signal: track mpesa_customers who had active subscriptions last month but not this month
Add revenue forecasting based on current subscriber count and average booking volume
Implement alert when available balance drops below a configurable threshold (payout risk management)
Add cohort analysis: revenue per organization to identify highest-value SACCOs for account management focus
Track exhausted Hyperledger enrollments as a compliance risk metric with admin notification

current_growth_features.detected_intent: Facilitates user onboarding by routing new users to the correct dashboard based on their declared intent (passenger, crew, operator, owner, org). This is the branching point that determines which growth loop a new user enters.
growth_potential: Add PostHog capture on intent selection to measure which roles are most commonly chosen and where drop-off occurs
Implement a guided onboarding checklist per intent type (e.g. 'operator' checklist: add vehicle → add driver → view dashboard)
Add progress persistence so users who abandon mid-onboarding can resume where they left off
A/B test intent label copy — 'operator' vs 'fleet manager' may resonate differently with target users
Add an 'I'm not sure' path that asks qualifying questions and recommends an intent, reducing wrong-role registrations
Track intent-to-activation rate: what % of users who select 'operator' actually complete their first GPS ping

current_growth_features.detected_intent: Enables data-driven decisions by providing a server-side analytics singleton for capturing events across SvelteKit server functions. Foundation for all product analytics, funnel tracking, and feature flag evaluation.
growth_potential: Instrument the invite redemption flow (token_viewed, account_created, role_activated) to measure invite conversion
Add feature flags via PostHog to enable A/B testing of onboarding copy, upgrade prompts, and alert messaging
Implement group analytics to track SACCO-level metrics (vehicles added, GPS pings, payments processed) not just user-level
Add session recording opt-in for ORG_CHAIR dashboard to identify UX friction in the finance and fleet views
Track the join-sacco funnel server-side: page_loaded → org_selected → form_submitted → request_approved
Set up PostHog cohorts for 'activated operators' (emitted first GPS ping) vs 'dormant operators' to power targeted re-engagement

current_growth_features.feature_name: Real-Time Operations Store with Incident Tracking
current_growth_features.detected_intent: Drives daily active engagement for OPERATIONS_MANAGER, DISPATCHER, and ROUTE_SUPERVISOR roles by providing real-time situational awareness. Urgent incidents and delayed trips create natural daily return behavior. The opsSummary KPI object is the core engagement hook.
growth_potential: Add push notifications for critical incidents (severity=CRITICAL) to drive immediate re-engagement even when dashboard is closed
Implement a daily operations summary email (trips completed, incidents resolved, on-time %) to create habitual return visits
Add gamification: 'streak' tracking for days with zero critical incidents to reinforce good operational behavior
Surface the urgentIncidents count as a badge on the navigation icon to create persistent engagement pull
Add shift handover notes feature so outgoing dispatchers can leave context for incoming shifts — increases stickiness
Track time-to-acknowledge for critical incidents in PostHog to measure operational responsiveness as a platform health metric

current_growth_features.detected_intent: Drives engagement by delivering real-time GPS position updates to fleet dashboards via Server-Sent Events. Live tracking is the core 'magic moment' for operators — seeing their vehicles move on a map is the primary value demonstration that drives retention.
growth_potential: Add connection quality indicator (connected/reconnecting/disconnected) in the UI so operators know when they're seeing live vs stale data
Implement geofence breach alerts via the SSE stream — vehicle leaving approved route triggers immediate notification
Track stream connection duration in PostHog to measure 'live tracking session length' as a core engagement metric
Add offline replay mode: when SSE disconnects, show last known positions with a timestamp so operators aren't left with a blank map
Surface GPS ping frequency per vehicle in the fleet dashboard to help operators identify trackers that need maintenance
Add a 'share live view' link that generates a read-only tracking URL for SACCO stakeholders who don't have accounts

current_growth_features.detected_intent: Drives organic acquisition through SEO-optimized content targeting Nairobi matatu operators, SACCO managers, and transit researchers. The blog covers operational pain points (empty return trips, NTSA compliance, GPS tracking) that map directly to the platform's value proposition.
growth_potential: Add structured data (JSON-LD Article schema) to blog posts to improve Google rich snippet eligibility
Implement email capture with a 'Get the quarterly data report' lead magnet mentioned in the empty-return-trips post
Add category-based RSS feeds so transit researchers and operators can subscribe to relevant content streams
Create a 'Request a demo' CTA at the end of each operations/data post to convert readers to leads
Add social sharing buttons optimized for WhatsApp (dominant in Kenya) to enable viral content distribution
Track blog-to-signup conversion in PostHog with UTM parameters to identify which content categories drive the most operator signups

current_growth_features.detected_intent: Facilitates operator onboarding by guiding users through GPS tracker pairing via BLE or QR scan. This is the physical activation step that connects real-world vehicles to the platform — completing the hardware-to-ledger chain.
growth_potential: Add a post-pairing celebration state with 'Your first GPS ping will appear within 60 seconds' to set expectations and create anticipation
Implement a pairing guide video or animated walkthrough for operators unfamiliar with BLE scanning
Add QR code generation in the admin panel so pre-printed QR stickers can ship with hardware — reducing pairing friction
Track pairing success/failure rate in PostHog to identify which tracker models or environments cause problems
Send a confirmation SMS to the operator's phone when the first GPS ping is received post-pairing — closes the activation loop
Add a 'pair another tracker' shortcut that pre-fills org context to make bulk fleet onboarding faster

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Contextual In-App Feature Gate & Upgrade Prompt System
growth_opportunities.description: There are no server-side enforcement gates or contextual upgrade modals anywhere in the codebase. Free-tier users who attempt to exceed plan limits (vehicles, route alerts, geofences, seats) see no prompt — they either silently succeed (revenue leakage) or hit an unhandled error. A reusable FeatureGate Svelte component backed by a server-side tier-check utility would intercept limit-exceeded actions and surface an upgrade modal with a one-tap M-Pesa STK push CTA. This is the highest-leverage free-to-paid conversion mechanism in PLG and is entirely absent. Distinct from the GPS flywheel's compliance-framed upgrade prompt — this covers all non-GPS feature limits across the full product surface.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: M-Pesa Dunning & Payment Failure Recovery Flow
growth_opportunities.description: When an M-Pesa STK push fails on subscription renewal, there is zero recovery logic: no retry, no SMS nudge, no grace period, no email fallback. Involuntary churn from payment failures is entirely unrecovered. Given that M-Pesa STK pushes have a meaningful failure rate (user dismissal, timeout, insufficient balance), a 3-step dunning sequence — (1) in-UI retry prompt immediately on failure, (2) Upstash Redis delayed SMS at day 1, (3) Resend email with manual payment link at day 3, with a 3-day grace period before downgrade — would recover a significant portion of at-risk subscribers. The Upstash Redis and Resend infrastructure is already in the stack and used for other notifications, making this a low-integration-cost, high-revenue-impact addition.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: SACCO Health & Benchmarking Report (Weekly Email Digest)
growth_opportunities.description: ORG_CHAIRs and fleet operators currently must log in to see their performance data. There is no push-based re-engagement mechanism for the finance and operations dashboards. A weekly email digest — sent via Resend, generated server-side using DuckDB aggregations — delivering top-line KPIs (total collected, on-time %, top route, fleet uptime, vs. prior week) would create a habitual re-engagement touchpoint without requiring a login. Including a 'your SACCO vs. platform average' benchmarking section creates social comparison motivation and surfaces upgrade value (e.g., 'Unlock route-level drill-down on Pro'). This is complementary to the GPS flywheel's ledger depth narrative — it re-engages operators on the financial and operational value layer, not the compliance layer.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: WhatsApp-Native Viral Sharing & Stakeholder Live View
growth_opportunities.description: The platform has no sharing or viral distribution mechanism. The GPS SSE stream already delivers live vehicle positions, but there is no way to share a read-only view with SACCO stakeholders, investors, or regulators who don't have accounts. A 'Share Live View' feature that generates a time-limited, token-authenticated read-only tracking URL — shareable via WhatsApp (the dominant communication channel in Kenya) — would expose the platform's core magic moment (vehicles moving on a map) to non-users, driving account creation. Blog posts could also include WhatsApp share buttons. This creates a viral acquisition loop entirely distinct from the GPS flywheel's operator-activation focus: it targets external stakeholders as the acquisition vector.

The matatu industry in Kenya is a tight-knit, high-trust network where word-of-mouth and peer recommendations dominate purchasing decisions. There is no formalized referral or affiliate mechanism in the codebase. A referral program — where existing ORG_CHAIRs or operators earn KES billing credits (e.g., 1 month free on their current plan) when a referred SACCO completes its first M-Pesa subscription payment — would formalize and incentivize the organic word-of-mouth already happening. Referral links could be generated from the org dashboard and shared via WhatsApp. PostHog would track the referral funnel. This is complementary to the GPS flywheel's operator acquisition path — it adds a peer-incentive layer on top of the existing activation flow.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Annual Subscription Plans with M-Pesa Lump-Sum Checkout
growth_opportunities.description: The pricing UI advertises a 'Save 20%' annual billing toggle, but the toggle is broken (references non-existent stripe_price_id fields) and no annual plan variants exist in the M-Pesa payment flow. Annual plans dramatically improve LTV, reduce involuntary churn from monthly renewal failures, and improve cash flow. Implementing annual plan variants (starter_annual, pro_annual, business_annual) at a 20% discount, wiring them into the M-Pesa STK push checkout with the correct lump-sum amounts, and fixing the pricing toggle would unlock a significant retention and revenue lever. This is a monetization fix distinct from the GPS flywheel's compliance-upgrade path — it targets the billing infrastructure layer.

The backend revenue config defines an 80% platform share on tips, but there is no tipping UI in any passenger-facing flow. This revenue stream is entirely dormant. A post-trip tipping screen — triggered after a reservation is marked complete in the passenger PWA, offering quick-select amounts (KES 20, KES 50, KES 100) via M-Pesa — would activate this revenue line. Even 10% tip adoption at average KES 40 per tipping transaction would meaningfully increase per-booking platform revenue. This is a net-new monetization surface that does not overlap with the GPS flywheel's operator-subscription focus.

The intent routing system branches users into role-specific dashboards, but there is no guided checklist or progress indicator after the branch point. An ORG_CHAIR who lands on their org dashboard has no clear next step beyond what they can discover by exploring. A persistent onboarding checklist component — rendered per role (e.g., Operator: Add vehicle → Pair GPS tracker → Add driver → View first trip) with completion state stored in the database — would reduce time-to-value and increase activation rates. Progress persistence ensures users who abandon mid-onboarding can resume. This complements the GPS flywheel's driver PWA activation path by addressing the operator-side activation gap.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Compliance Module Add-On for Regulators & Planners
growth_opportunities.description: The platform has dedicated dashboards for REGULATOR, PLANNER, COMPLIANCE_OFFICER, and ACCOUNTANT roles, but these roles appear nowhere in the pricing tiers — the entire B2G and institutional buyer segment is unmonetized. A 'Compliance Module' add-on (KES 5,000-15,000/month per organization) providing regulators with NTSA-formatted compliance exports, Hyperledger audit trails, route adherence reports, and anonymized fleet statistics would create a high-margin B2G revenue stream. This is a distinct product tier from the operator-focused subscription plans and targets an entirely different buyer with a procurement budget.

The platform collects rich operational telemetry (GPS pings, trip completion, revenue variance, incident severity) but has no proactive alerting layer that pushes insights to operators without requiring them to log in. An anomaly detection engine — using DuckDB aggregations to identify vehicles significantly below revenue target, GPS trackers that have gone silent, or routes with unusual delay patterns — paired with SMS delivery via M-Pesa's SMS gateway or a dedicated SMS provider, would drive daily active use by making the platform feel like an active operations partner rather than a passive dashboard. This is distinct from the GPS flywheel's V/T ratio instrumentation — it targets the revenue and operations layer, not the GPS coverage health layer.

The Business plan is priced at KES 4,900 per user per month, but the M-Pesa STK push sends a single fixed amount regardless of team size. Multi-seat Business customers are severely undercharged. A seat-count selection step before Business plan checkout — calculating total = KES 4,900 × seats with volume discount tiers — would close this revenue leakage. This is a billing infrastructure fix with direct revenue impact, distinct from the GPS flywheel's subscription conversion path.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Anonymized Transit Data API for Urban Planners & Researchers
growth_opportunities.description: The platform accumulates uniquely valuable urban mobility data: GPS traces, trip patterns, passenger volumes, route adherence, and compliance events across Nairobi's matatu network. This data is entirely unmonetized. A 'Transit Intelligence' API or data export product — targeting PLANNER and REGULATOR roles, urban research institutions, and county governments at KES 20,000-50,000/month — would create a high-margin B2G revenue stream with near-zero marginal cost. DuckDB is already in the stack and well-suited for the aggregation queries needed. This is a complementary revenue stream that monetizes data generated by the GPS flywheel without competing with it.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Blog Lead Magnet & Email Capture Funnel
growth_opportunities.description: The blog targets NTSA compliance, route efficiency, and GPS tracking pain points — topics directly relevant to the buyer persona — but has no email capture mechanism. A lead magnet (e.g., 'Kenya Matatu Route Performance Report Q1 2025' downloadable PDF) with an email capture gate at the end of high-traffic blog posts would build a nurture list of warm prospects. A drip email sequence (Resend) converting blog readers to demo requests or free trial signups would close the content-to-pipeline gap. UTM tracking in PostHog would attribute signups to specific content pieces. This is a top-of-funnel acquisition play complementary to the GPS flywheel's activation focus.

revenue_leakage.issue: Fleet Manager feature is available on the Free tier with up to 5 vehicles — this is a core operational feature that should be paywalled or significantly restricted to drive upgrades
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Limit Free tier Fleet Manager to 1-2 vehicles maximum, or remove it entirely from Free and make it a Starter+ feature. Fleet management is a high-value operational tool that fleet operators will pay for — giving it away on Free removes the primary upgrade incentive for the OWNER/VEHICLE_OWNER segment.

revenue_leakage.issue: Insights Snapshot analytics is available on the Free tier — analytics is typically a strong paid conversion driver and should not be freely available without restriction
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Remove Insights Snapshot from Free or severely limit it (e.g., last 7 days only, no drill-down). Analytics is a key value proposition for operators and fleet managers — restricting it creates a clear upgrade path to Starter/Pro.

revenue_leakage.issue: The pricing_module.svelte billing toggle is broken — getDisplayPrice() and getDisplayInterval() reference plan.stripe_price_id which does not exist on the PricingPlan interface, causing the annual discount calculation to silently fail for all plans. The 'Save 20%' chip appears but no price changes occur.
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Fix the annual billing toggle to use the correct field (mpesaAmount or a new annual_mpesa_amount field). The 20% annual discount is a strong conversion and retention lever — users who see annual pricing are more likely to commit. Add annual plan variants with correct amounts to the pricing_plans.ts config.

revenue_leakage.issue: No annual subscription option is implemented in the M-Pesa payment flow — only monthly plans exist, missing a significant LTV and retention opportunity despite the UI advertising a 20% annual discount
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Add annual plan variants (e.g., starter_annual, pro_annual, business_annual) with a 20% discount as advertised in the UI. Annual plans improve cash flow, reduce churn, and increase LTV. Wire them into the M-Pesa STK push flow with appropriate annual amounts and fix the toggle in pricing_module.svelte.

revenue_leakage.issue: No in-app feature gates or upgrade prompts — users who hit free tier limits (3 route alerts, 5 geofences, 1 seat) receive no contextual upgrade prompt driving them to a paid plan. Free tier limits exist only as marketing copy with no enforcement or conversion mechanism.
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement server-side enforcement of tier limits and build a reusable FeatureGate component that triggers upgrade modals when free users attempt to exceed limits. Show upgrade CTAs contextually (e.g., 'You have used 3/3 Route Alerts — upgrade to Starter for 25') rather than only on the billing page. This is the most effective free-to-paid conversion mechanism.

revenue_leakage.issue: Free tier has no vehicle limit enforcement in code — the pricing plan lists '5 vehicles' but there is no enforcement mechanism visible in the codebase, meaning free users can potentially add unlimited vehicles without upgrading
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement server-side enforcement of vehicle limits per subscription tier. Add a check in vehicle creation endpoints that queries the user's current plan and vehicle count before allowing inserts. Without enforcement, the free tier limits are marketing copy only and users have no reason to upgrade.

revenue_leakage.issue: The reservation fee is only KES 19 per seat — at this price point, platform revenue per transaction (KES 15) may not cover M-Pesa transaction costs, especially for single-seat bookings, resulting in negative-margin transactions
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Review the KES 19 reservation fee against M-Pesa transaction costs (typically KES 0-33 depending on amount tier). Consider raising the fee to KES 25-30 to maintain positive margin, or implement a minimum booking value. Also consider a percentage-based fee model tied to fare value rather than a flat fee to scale revenue with transaction size.

revenue_leakage.issue: Business plan at KES 4,900/user/month is priced per user but the M-Pesa STK push sends a single fixed amount — there is no mechanism to collect per-seat pricing for multi-user Business plans, causing severe revenue leakage for any team with more than one user
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement a seat-count selection step before the Business plan checkout that calculates total = KES 4,900 × seats (with volume discount logic applied). The current flow charges a flat KES 4,900 regardless of team size, causing significant revenue leakage for multi-seat Business customers.

revenue_leakage.issue: Stripe integration code still exists and is actively imported (subscription_helpers.server.ts with full Stripe SDK usage) while M-Pesa is the active payment processor — this dead code suggests incomplete migration and potential for split or confused payment paths that could result in uncharged users
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Audit whether any routes still call Stripe subscription helpers. If fully migrated to M-Pesa, remove Stripe code to eliminate confusion and potential accidental routing failures. If Stripe is needed for international or card-paying users, make it an explicit secondary payment method with clear routing logic and ensure both paths are tested end-to-end.

revenue_leakage.issue: The FAQ on the pricing page references Stripe test cards ('Use Stripe test card 4242...') despite the platform being M-Pesa only — this creates confusion and signals an incomplete or inconsistent product to potential customers, reducing conversion trust
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Update the FAQ to remove Stripe references and replace with M-Pesa sandbox or testing instructions. Outdated payment copy erodes trust and may cause potential customers to abandon the signup flow when they see mismatched payment method references.

revenue_leakage.issue: No trial period or freemium-to-paid conversion mechanism — users can stay on the free tier indefinitely with no time pressure, trial expiry, or urgency nudging them toward paid plans
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement a 14-day Pro trial for new signups to let users experience premium features before reverting to Free. Add time-based upgrade prompts (e.g., 'Your Pro trial ends in 3 days') and email sequences targeting free users who have used the product but not converted after 7, 12, and 14 days.

revenue_leakage.issue: The billing page only shows upgrade options when the user has no active subscription — active subscribers on lower tiers see no upsell path to higher tiers, missing cross-sell and upgrade revenue from existing paying customers
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Show a plan comparison and upgrade CTA for active subscribers on lower tiers (e.g., a Starter subscriber should see a prominent 'Upgrade to Pro' option with feature highlights). Add a 'Change Plan' button that shows the full pricing module with current plan highlighted and a clear value proposition for upgrading.

revenue_leakage.issue: No payment failure recovery flow — when an M-Pesa STK push fails on subscription renewal, there is no automated retry logic, SMS or email dunning sequence, or grace period before downgrade. Involuntary churn from payment failures is entirely unrecovered.
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement a 3-step dunning flow: (1) immediate retry prompt in UI when STK push fails, (2) SMS reminder at day 1, (3) email with manual payment link at day 3, with a 3-day grace period before downgrading to Free on subscription renewal failure. Failed payments are one of the most recoverable churn sources.

revenue_leakage.issue: API Access is gated behind Pro+ plans but there is no API usage metering, rate limiting enforcement, or API add-on product — enterprise API consumers have no way to pay for higher API quotas and overages go unmonetized
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Define and enforce API rate limits per tier (e.g., 1,000 calls/day on Pro, 10,000 on Business, unlimited on Enterprise). Offer an API add-on pack for Pro users who need more calls. API metering creates a natural usage-based revenue stream and upgrade trigger for high-volume users.

revenue_leakage.issue: The platform has multiple high-value roles (REGULATOR, PLANNER, COMPLIANCE_OFFICER, ACCOUNTANT) with dedicated dashboards but no differentiated pricing for these specialized roles — they are not represented in any pricing tier, meaning this B2G segment is entirely unmonetized
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Consider role-specific pricing or add-on modules for regulatory and compliance features (REGULATOR, COMPLIANCE_OFFICER, PLANNER). These users have specialized, high-value needs and work within organizations with procurement budgets. A 'Compliance Module' add-on at KES 5,000-15,000/month could capture significant B2G and B2B revenue.

revenue_leakage.issue: Tips are split 80% to platform but there is no in-app tipping UI visible in any passenger-facing flow — this revenue stream exists in the backend revenue config but is entirely unsurfaced to users, leaving it effectively inactive
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Build a prominent post-trip tipping screen in the passenger booking flow with suggested tip amounts (KES 20, 50, 100) as quick-select options triggered after a reservation is marked complete. Even a 10% tip adoption rate among bookings would meaningfully increase platform revenue given the 80% platform share.

revenue_leakage.issue: No usage tracking or usage-based billing — the platform collects rich telemetry (trips, bookings, geofences, route alerts) but does not monetize usage overages or offer usage-based pricing, meaning power users on free or low tiers receive unlimited value without paying for it
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Consider adding usage-based add-ons (e.g., pay-per-booking above plan limits, additional geofence packs at KES 200/10 geofences, extra route alert bundles). This captures revenue from power users who exceed limits rather than losing them to churn or free tier abuse.

revenue_leakage.issue: The /billing/manage route silently redirects to /account/billing with no functionality — users expecting a billing portal with invoice downloads, payment method management, and renewal history find nothing, reducing perceived value of paid plans and increasing support ticket volume
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Build out the billing management page with: (1) downloadable payment receipts and invoices, (2) subscription renewal date and auto-renewal toggle, (3) plan change history. A professional billing experience increases trust, reduces support tickets, and reduces churn among paying customers who judge product quality by operational polish.

revenue_leakage.issue: No referral or affiliate program — the platform serves a tight-knit network-effect market (matatu operators, SACCOs, drivers) where word-of-mouth is the dominant acquisition channel, but organic referrals are not captured or incentivized, leaving viral growth potential untapped
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement a referral program where existing operators earn KES credits (e.g., 1 month free on their current plan) for referring new SACCO or organization signups that achieve first payment. Given the tight-knit nature of the matatu industry, formalizing and incentivizing referrals would accelerate paid conversions at low CAC.

revenue_leakage.issue: No revenue from anonymized transit data products — the platform collects uniquely valuable GPS traces, trip patterns, passenger volumes, route adherence data, and compliance events that urban planners, government regulators, and researchers would pay for, but this data is entirely unmonetized
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Develop an anonymized transit data product for government planners, urban researchers, and regulators. A 'Transit Data API' or 'Analytics Export' subscription targeting PLANNER and REGULATOR roles at KES 20,000-50,000/month would create a high-margin B2G revenue stream with minimal marginal cost, leveraging data the platform already collects.
